ANAT.definition_en: Mentions of anatomical entities across scales, including organs, tissues, cell types, subcellular components, body fluids, and named anatomical regions. Excludes diseases, molecules, experimental conditions, and whole organisms.

final_task_goal: This task builds a single-label anatomical NER resource that prioritizes ontology-aligned normalization and linkage for large-scale literature mining and database integration. * Document pool and source: Documents are drawn from English-language biomedical literature, including PubMed abstracts and PubMed Central Open Access full-text excerpts. * Purpose of NER: Identify contiguous spans that denote anatomical entities, assign the Anatomy label consistently across biological scales, and enable mapping to controlled vocabularies and ontologies such as UMLS and OBO-derived resources. * Entity types: A single category is used—Anatomy (ANAT)—covering organs, tissues, cell types, subcellular components, body fluids, and named anatomical regions. * Downstream applications: The annotations and resulting taggers support entity normalization and cross-resource linking, powering literature-scale tagging and integration into search and analytics services, and supplying reliable inputs to subsequent biomedical IE tasks.
